text: Given valid credentials and a generic resource type (e.g. documents), When delete_attachment is called, Then it sends DELETE /{resource_type}/{resource_id}/relationships/attachments with body {"data": [{"type": "attachments", "attributes": {"id": <attachment_id>}}]} and returns {"id": "<attachment_id>", "deleted": true}.
Given resource_type="flexible_assets", When delete_attachment is called, Then it sends the same DELETE shape against the flexible-assets path and returns the same success envelope.
Given IT Glue returns 404 for the attachment id, When delete_attachment is called, Then it returns {"error": {"code": "not_found", ...}} rather than raising.
Given the X-ITGlue-API-Key header is missing, When delete_attachment is called, Then it returns {"error": {"code": "not_configured", ...}} rather than raising.
notes: Covered generically via the shared run() path (asserted today against other tools); delete_attachment goes through the same run() helper unmodified, so no per-tool duplicate is required, but a direct assertion against delete_attachment itself is preferred for a destructive tool -- see test_delete_attachment_missing_credentials if the dev leg adds one.

text: Given IT Glue returns 429 then 204, When delete_attachment is called, Then it retries once honouring Retry-After and returns {"id": ..., "deleted": true}; given IT Glue returns 403, Then it returns {"error": {"code": "unauthorized", "retryable": false}}.
notes: Error-code mapping and retry/backoff are exercised generically against other tools through the shared ITGlueClient.request() path; delete_attachment reuses that path unmodified. A dedicated retry test against delete_attachment itself is listed because it is the only destructive new tool in this ticket and its 204-on-success path (api.py's 'no content -> None' branch) is worth a direct assertion.

text: Given tools/list is queried, When delete_attachment is registered, Then it is present with destructiveHint true and readOnlyHint false, has no agent_id parameter, is listed in README's Tools table, and no existing tool loses a name or parameter.
notes: Requires adding a delete_attachment entry to tests/fixtures/tools_baseline.json and bumping the two hardcoded tool-count assertions in tests/test_middleware.py (37 -> 38) in the same change.
